findings.title: Cleanup skipped when channel.stop() raises
findings.problem: _close_channel calls channel.stop() and channel.cleanup(kill=False) inside one try block. If stop() raises, cleanup is never attempted. run() then sets channel = None, so the finally-block _close_channel retries nothing. The unit test test_close_channel_swallows_errors asserts cleanup is not called.
findings.impact: The task requires exchange-folder cleanup to complete before any export or changed-files snapshot. With stop() failing, the folder stays in the pod workdir through the download phase. ToolCallChannel.stop() has little that can raise today, so reachability is unconfirmed and severity is capped at major, but the guarantee is structurally absent and locked in by a test.
findings.recommendation: Use try/finally so cleanup(kill=False) always runs after stop(), each step logging its own failure. Invert the test to assert cleanup is still called when stop() raises.

findings.title: Timeout messages report wrong widened budget
findings.problem: _wait_for_pod_running, _wait_for_sentinel and _wait_for_completion still format execution_timeout + _DEADLINE_BUFFER_SECONDS in their timeout errors, although the deadline is now _budget_seconds(tool_calling_timeout). The _wait_for_completion docstring still describes the old budget. No test checks the message text.
findings.impact: When a tool-calling run times out, users and agents are told it exceeded e.g. 65s although the Job was allowed 180s, which misleads diagnosis.
findings.recommendation: Compute the budget once in run() and pass it (or the formatted value) to the wait helpers, or derive it from the deadline. Add a test with tool_calling_timeout above execution_timeout that asserts the widened number in the message.

findings.title: Bridge folder not excluded from explicit exports
findings.problem: Bridge-folder filtering exists only in _download_changed_files. _download_exports, which serves JobResult.exported_files, filters nothing, and the caller's _validate_export_paths only checks for workdir escape and blocked system prefixes, not BRIDGE_DIR_NAME. No test makes channel.cleanup fail inside run() or covers a normal-cleanup case.
findings.impact: The required criterion says the bridge folder must never appear in changed_files or exports even if cleanup fails. If cleanup fails, a requested export_files entry under .codemie_bridge is downloaded and stored. The criterion is partial and unproven by tests.
findings.recommendation: Skip or reject any path whose first segment is BRIDGE_DIR_NAME in _download_exports (and/or _validate_export_paths). Add run()-level tests where channel.cleanup raises or fails and bridge paths appear in the snapshot and in export_files, asserting neither reaches JobResult.

findings.title: Tool-calling timeout has no upper bound
findings.problem: With the session-lifetime clamp removed, _resolve_tool_calling_limit rejects only values <= 0. The admin pattern ^[1-9][0-9]*$ accepts arbitrarily large values, and the result flows into int(_budget_seconds(...)) for activeDeadlineSeconds, the shared wait deadline and the held Job semaphore slot.
findings.impact: An oversized value can exceed the Kubernetes int64 field, so Job creation is rejected and every tool-calling run fails. Otherwise it pins a capacity slot for a very long time. Reachability depends on admin-supplied config and on validation outside the read window, so it was not confirmed.
findings.recommendation: Clamp to a documented maximum (for example MAX_TOOL_CALLING_SECONDS) in _resolve_tool_calling_limit and log a warning when clamped. Treat non-finite values as disabled.
